headlines.article_text: Boeing CEO: need 'couple more years' to repair finances before new jet Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Boeing CEO Kelly Ortberg told CNBC Monday that the planemaker will need "a couple more years" to repair its finances before launching a new commercial jet. Airline customers are telling Boeing to focus on improving the reliability and production of its current lineup rather than introducing a new model, Ortberg said. Eventually, a new plane to better compete with rival Airbus's A320 family of jets will likely be crucial for Boeing to secure future business. In this article AIR-FR BA Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 5:11 05:11 Boeing CEO: New Air Force One most complex twin-aisle plane we've ever built Squawk Box Europe Boeing CEO Kelly Ortberg told CNBC Monday that the planemaker will need "a couple more years" to repair its finances before launching a new commercial jet, signaling that the company is focused more on stabilizing its existing business rather than rushing to develop a successor to its best-selling 737 MAX. Boeing must clear three hurdles before committing to a new aircraft program, Ortberg told CNBC's Phil LeBeau at the Farnborough International Airshow in the U.K. "First of all, we have to be ready, and part of that is getting our financial house in order, and we're working on that," Ortberg said.
